title: Velox Payments — contract refresh & edge provisioning checkpoint
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on an upcoming contract refresh. Customer is evaluating a 2x capacity uplift, APAC region add, and a private VPC pilot. Main concerns: latency targets for fraud models, regulatory data residency in APAC, and encryption/KMS integration. Action: Redwood to send tailored pricing, security pack, and proposed pilot SOW for on-prem/VPC path.
next_steps: Redwood to send 2 options pricing (hosted vs dedicated with burst) by 2025-05-23
Share SOC2+ISO pack and KMS integration guide by 2025-05-23
Schedule 90-minute technical bench on 2025-05-28 for latency tests in APAC
Draft 8-week pilot SOW for VPC/on-prem path by 2025-05-26
action_items: Nina Park: send pricing and security pack by 2025-05-23
Luis Moreno: prepare bench plan and APAC latency test checklist by 2025-05-26
Aisha Khan: draft pilot SOW + kickoff template by 2025-05-26
Samir Patel: provide current token volumes and peak TPS data by 2025-05-24
transcript:
[00:00] Nina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see Samir, Elena, Tom and Jia are on. we wanted to make this a quick checkpoint ahead of your renewal to make sure the uplift and region plan fit your latency and compliance needs.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yeah thanks Nina. Real quick, we are planning to renew in early June and want clarity on two things — a 2x capacity bump and an APAC region. also curious about whether we should do Dedicated or VPC pilot.
[00:25] Nina Park: Great, that's exactly what we want to cover. Luis from our SE team will go through latency and the staging plan, and Aisha will cover pilot logistics.
[00:34] Luis Moreno: hi all, brief from infra side — the fraud scoring workload you described is bursty at end of day and needs sub-120ms p99 for short sequences; is that still right?
[00:42] Elena Ross: yes, for the most part, we need p99 under 100–120ms for the model path used in production for pre-auth checks, longer sequences allowed for batch risk runs. sometimes the token length varies, we saw spikes.
[00:53] Jia Li: and we have regulatory constraints in singapore and japan, so data residency and key management are important, we can't have unencrypted KV caches leaving region.
[01:05] Nina Park: understood. quick note on options — hosted + APAC region is fastest to get up, Dedicated reserved pools give predictable throughput and cost, Private VPC/on-prem gives you control for compliance. we'll map tradeoffs.
[01:18] Tom Briggs: procurement question — if we go dedicated, does that change billing terms, and are there exit clauses?
[01:24] Nina Park: yes dedicated is a committed contract; we can do monthly or annual commitments with a standard termination clause that's typical for reserved capacity. we'll include contract language options in the pricing doc.
[01:33] Luis Moreno: wanted to show a quick slide but I'll just summarize — for the fraud model with short context (<=64 tokens) we can hit p95 in 25–40ms on our c5-style nodes, p99 depends on burst controls and batching, so we need to tune continuous batching and prefix cache to meet p99.
[01:50] Elena Ross: when you say prefix cache, are we talking Redwood managed cache or something that sits inside our VPC?
[01:57] Luis Moreno: good question — both options exist. hosted uses Redwood-managed prefix/KV caching with regional controls, VPC gives you a customer-managed cache layer. note: cross-region cache replication increases latency so for APAC we suggest region-local cache.
[02:10] Samir Patel: okay, replication is a no-go for regulatory datasets. we also need KMS integration — we use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS today.
[02:18] Nina Park: we support KMS integrations — our security pack includes docs for AWS KMS and Vault patterns. for VPC/private deployment we can surface HSM/KMS handoff and key policies. we'll attach the integration guide.
[02:30] Speaker 3: (muted) i think the other thing is burst capacity, like if we do 2x base commit can we have burst on top?
[02:36] Nina Park: yes, we offer burst pools for Dedicated customers, and hosted customers can enable burst for an overage fee. we'll show cost comparisons in the pricing options.
[02:45] Tom Briggs: procurement follow-up — what's the SLA difference between hosted and dedicated?
[02:50] Aisha Khan: hosted has a standard uptime SLA, dedicated can come with an elevated SLA and custom latency SLO language for an enterprise plan. also observability retention is an add-on.
[03:01] Jia Li: we need audit trails, fine-grained RBAC and SSO — can you do SAML and SCIM sync?
[03:06] Nina Park: yes SAML + SCIM supported, RBAC with role templates, and we send audit logs to our logging endpoint or to your S3/secure bucket. we'll include sample configs in the security pack.
[03:17] Elena Ross: i want to talk cost — some competitors pitched lower per-token costs but higher latency. can you walk us through cost per inference vs p99 tradeoffs?
[03:27] Luis Moreno: absolutely — there is a classic trade: quantization and larger batch sizes lower per-token cost but increase latency. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per-workload and we can run a small sweep in the bench to find the sweet spot for your fraud model.
[03:41] Samir Patel: how long would the bench take and do we need to provide a dataset?
[03:47] Luis Moreno: bench usually 60–90 minutes of orchestrated runs per region plus some tuning time. we ask for a representative prompt set and sample traffic. we can anonymize or use synthetic traffic if you prefer.
[03:57] Nina Park: next steps wise we propose two commercial lanes: 1) Hosted APAC add + usage uplift with burst enabled, 2) Dedicated reserved 2x capacity in US + pilot VPC in APAC for compliance. we'll price both and outline pilot SOW.
[04:12] Tom Briggs: and pilot SOW — how long, what does success look like?
[04:17] Aisha Khan: standard VPC pilot is 6–8 weeks: week 0 onboarding, weeks 1–2 baseline bench, weeks 3–5 integration and validation, final week report and runbook handover. success criteria: p99 under 120ms in APAC for pre-auth path, KV cache encryption in-region, integration with your KMS, and runbook for scale.
[04:36] Jia Li: we also need a data retention/PII deletion policy for logs — can logs be redacted before leaving the region?
[04:43] Luis Moreno: yes per-route log redaction is supported and we can configure retention windows per workspace. we'll include options in the security doc.
[04:52] Speaker 2: some clarity on model variants — can Redwood auto-fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained?
[04:57] Nina Park: yes we have automated fallback policies — you can configure routing by latency or cost, and fallbacks to quantized or smaller family models are supported. we'll show examples in the tech appendix.
[05:07] Elena Ross: i want to flag an internal timeline — we need final procurement by June 9 to match our quarter budget. so pricing and SOW in next week is critical.
[05:16] Nina Park: noted, we'll prioritize. Luis, can you commit to the bench session on 5/28?
[05:21] Luis Moreno: yes i'll run the bench with our infra team and can slot 90 minutes starting 2025-05-28 08:00 PT.
[05:28] Samir Patel: okay, and a question on encryption in-flight — how are TLS certs handled for private deployments?
[05:34] Nina Park: for private we hand you cert rotation guides; if you want mutual TLS we can enable mTLS and coordinate cert trust stores into your VPC.
[05:43] Tom Briggs: procurement needs the contract redline, do you have a sample enterprise amendment?
[05:48] Nina Park: yes we'll attach a sample amendment and we can accept typical data processing addenda; legal can engage if needed.
[05:55] Jia Li: one last technical — for APAC edge nodes do you offer GPU-backed instances or CPU-only? we need low latency for small models so GPU may help.
[06:03] Luis Moreno: APAC edge supports both; GPU-backed give better p99 for small context models if the sequence is compute bound. we'll lay out expected p95/p99 numbers per instance type.
[06:14] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) are there compliance certifications in APAC?
[06:18] Nina Park: our platform is SOC 2 Type II and we're pursuing local certifications per region; we'll put a note in the security pack for any region-specific coverage.
[06:27] Elena Ross: okay, i think we have a good path. can you summarize the two lanes and next steps?
[06:33] Nina Park: sure — lane A hosted: add APAC region, uplift usage by 2x, enable burst and Redwood-managed caching; faster provisioning, lower upfront but slightly variable cost. Lane B dedicated + VPC pilot: committed 2x reserved capacity with burst pool and a VPC pilot in APAC for compliance, higher commitment, predictable throughput, custom SLA. Next steps: we'll send pricing and security pack by 5/23, bench on 5/28, pilot SOW draft by 5/26, you (Samir) send token volumes by 5/24.
[06:57] Samir Patel: sounds good. one last thing — can you include migration/rollout runbook for traffic shifting?
[07:03] Aisha Khan: yes we'll include a blue/green rollout plan and can do a short playbook session during pilot.
[07:09] Nina Park: thanks everyone. quick recap of owners: Nina pricing/security, Luis bench and tech appendix, Aisha SOW and runbook, Samir volume data. we'll reconvene after bench.
[07:20] Tom Briggs: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[07:22] Nina Park: thanks all, talk soon.
[07:25] End of recording.
